Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Primary request: Make a fresh, plausible fully grown adult photograph of the SAME individual female Miniature American Shepherd shown in these TWO REAL puppy photographs, aged about 18–24 months. This is an illustrative adult possibility.
Input images: image 1 is the latest real portrait with the puppy in a basket, authoritative for face and iris details and visible flank pattern. Image 2 is the earlier real photograph of the SAME puppy held by a person, supplying chest, legs, paw markings, head and ear pattern. These are the ONLY visual references. Do not use, reproduce or derive from any earlier AI image. Build the adult from the real dog's individual markings rather than a generic breed template.
Identity constraints: Map the actual copper, black, white and silver boundaries visible in both photographs onto an anatomically mature dog. Keep each facial side's asymmetry, the width and extent of white markings, cheek and eyebrow copper, nose pigmentation, ear pattern, chest white, tan legs and paw white as evidenced. Fur becomes an adult coat but colour patches do not relocate arbitrarily. For the body, show the SAME flank visible in image 1 and preserve the relative positions and shapes of its observed large black patches against the silver base. Occluded back, hind legs and tail need plausible completion rather than a claim of exact prediction. Never substitute a near-solid black saddle or turn this into a solid-white dog.
Eyes: Study the irises of this individual in both real photographs. Carry the observed natural blue tone and any subtle per-eye variation into this adult possibility. Keep realistic pupils, natural catchlights and crisp iris texture; do not homogenize every dog into the same pale grey iris, oversaturate, create glowing eyes, invent brown/amber sectors or impose heterochromia. Adult eye shape and muzzle proportions must be realistic, not enlarged puppy eyes.
Composition: Refined landscape 3:2 photograph pair. Left panel approximately 60%: complete adult standing naturally, body in a three-quarter flank view with head turned toward the camera, all four paws, ears and entire natural tail comfortably inside the frame. Right panel approximately 40%: detailed head and upper chest of the SAME adult dog with identical face markings in both panels. Clean narrow divider. Neutral quiet outdoor setting with soft daylight, natural colour balance and photographic depth of field. Avoid distracting props, the puppy basket, plush toys, flowers, the holding person, collars and other dogs. True-to-life compact athletic adult build and moderately feathered coat, not a giant heavily coated show Aussie.

The nose is black. The centre forehead/nose bridge is sparse pale-grey merle flecking over copper, NOT a wide solid white blaze. Do not enlarge the tiny pale central detail into puppy 02's broad stripe or puppy 03's white tuft.
